newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate plummets in post-election calm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate plummets in post-election calm.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened down a sharp 289 basis points at 17.76 percent on Monday.
Dealers and analysts said market relief over the relative lack of conflict and fraud allegations in Sunday's mid-term elections boosted confidence and fuelled demand for paper.
"The market is in a great mood above all because the elections had been exerting upside pressure on rates," a fixed-income analyst said.
"But after everything went ahead smoothly and results were respected, the market is confident, and that's why demand for paper is so heavy," he added.

Mexicans voted on Sunday for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post had been filled by a presidential nominee.
Preliminary results showed President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) had lost overall control of the lower house for the first time since 1929.
The PRI also lost Mexico City, the country's nerve centre, to Cuauhtmoc Crdenas, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
Analysts stressed the relative lack of allegations of fraud, that have often marred elections in the past, were almost as important as the results themselves.
"Crdenas' win has been well received, the peso is strong, rates are down and the markets are doing well," a trader said.
